beta_new: The first pitch climbs the face past a horizontal crack to a bolt, then continues on the face, with a runout, to a ledge. The second pitch is easy face and a wide crack straight up to the top.
Ascend flakes and edges, clipping one bolt, up toward the pale scar. Though a direct finish was the goal, the line instead swings leftward round to the west side for the finish.
A wide, fairly tidy chimney made by the scimitar-shaped flake and the buttress on its right. Chips Ahoy's bolts can be clipped for protection here as well.
Start from the big detached flake on the west face. The first pitch climbs the face to a bolt, then continues rightward past another bolt to a crack and an overhang.
Scramble to the upper south face, then climb a crack that leans left to a stance. Leave it by the face, clipping a bolt, and go to the top.

Mount a flake at the base of the wall, follow a broken, thin crack, then step onto the face and clip a bolt beside the arete on its left. Keep going on the face past another bolt, where the crux sits.
Begin at the rectangular north face and climb the steep face, clipping two bolts, to the top.
Start on the boulder's northeast side, just right of the corner, and climb the face with two bolts to the top.
Share the opening with High Noon through the third bolt, then leave that route's cracks and go up the bulges instead.
Climb the face to a horizontal break under a roof, and pull the roof by way of the thin crack and xenolith. Above, trace broken seams, clipping a bolt, to the top.

Start up the face, clipping two bolts, then cross about ten feet leftward to a third. Move straight up toward a little ledge with a fourth bolt beside it, then traverse left into a crack and follow it to the notch where you belay.

Begin as for Alley Oop, but after mantling into the chimney, step left and clip a bolt to reach a crack. When you arrive at the big roof's left margin, traverse rightward over its lip and finish up the arete.
Start in the chimney that splits the formation, clipping a bolt, then transfer leftward to the face and finish with three more bolts.
Climb the face off the boulder, which holds the crux, to thin cracks both horizontal and vertical. Then follow cracks and the face, clipping a bolt, to the top.
Climb the face by way of horizontal breaks and some vertical cracks to the top. Take care, as the protection is thin.
Climb the face past a bolt to a roof, pull over it, and clip a pair of bolts on the way to the top.
Go up and rightward on the face, clipping three bolts through the crux, to reach the arete. Then continue on the face to its right as far as the rappel anchor.
Climb the small prow on the face with three bolts, then keep going up the face past one more bolt to the top.
Take the wall's face, clipping two bolts and working around the embedded xenoliths, straight up to the top.

Follow its salad-named neighbor as far as the ledge, then step left and finish on the upper half of the harder route. Despite the matching grade it is the easier of the two, and five draws are left in place.
A short bouldery start gets you up to bolt number one, after which positive holds lead straight up. The crux is a mantle up to the top shelf.
Easy-going moves take you up to bolt one, then the steep face continues on solid holds. At the shelf, stretch way out across the roof to the jugs above.
Expect something hard at each bolt, so there is no real rest on the way up.
Climb the offwidth crack that splits the face, then shift rightward to top out at a neighbor's anchor.

moves.from: Bring big cams, from a #2 up to a #6.

beta_new: The start is cruxy, then a haul on jugs follows. Angle off rightward around the orange overhang, and the anchors are guarded by a second crux higher on the slab.

From the Westmin lot, climb switchbacks to Arnica Lake and then follow the long ridge over several bumps; a roughly 6 m Class 3 ledge near Terror Peak is the main exposure there. Descend steeply to the Carter Lake area, continue past Opal Lake and over a col to the Schjelderup lakes, then drop into the gully between the Schjelderup and Burman drainages. Cross to Moraine Lake, climb the south and southeast scree slopes toward the north end of the summit ridge, and ascend the steep couloir (roughly 55 degrees in places, with a narrow line beside the snow). A short scramble of about 50 m finishes on the summit.

From the campsite, go up alpine slabs to the glacier and cross it, watching for crevasses. Reach the ledge on the east side of the glacier; the step up to it is fourth class on loose rock, and the ledge is narrow and exposed, with bolt anchors that allow a handline. Beyond the ledge the north ridge is easy scrambling on solid quartzite to a final snow wall and cornice below the summit.

Climb steeply through forest and meadows, crossing creeks, to the upper mountain. The upper scramble is hard to follow: expect route-finding, a downclimb into a notch, and a crux in chimneys. Plenty of water is available lower down.
Beyond the last bolt, heading directly upward is considerably harder; trending right and then returning leftward to the anchors is the easier way.
Trends leftward up the formation's northern flank past five bolts to a bolted lower-off. The fourth bolt is missing its hanger, so carry something to deal with that.
Begin up a brief crack on the tower's left side, then angle rightward and continue upward past a pair of bolts.
Start about twenty feet right of its neighbor on the left, clip three bolts, and arrive at the upper corner shared with that line.

Angles rightward along the corner starting from the terrace, with seven bolts on the way and a sizable runout on the ramp near the top before the belay. Easy fourth to low fifth class leads leftward and upward to the formation's summit.
Begins at the right-hand end of the northeast aspect; from the gully, clip the first bolt in passing to reach the main wall, and watch for slightly friable rock low down.
Small cams placed in the arched crack off to the side can supplement the first bolt.

Begin beside the pair of ramps that cross in a big X, working leftward over a vegetated ramp system and then a right-facing corner; a tension traverse rightward beneath a dike reaches flakes and another vegetated ramp.

Continue along that ramp upward and rightward to a wide vertical corner, then face climb beside a wide crack with questionable protection to reach the cave where the X crosses.

From the cave, a wide crack heads up and right, followed by a rightward traverse beneath a roof, then a leftward traverse under a second roof and a pendulum into a shallow chimney, whose rear cracks finish the route.
Starts beside the picnic table with a thin, sparsely protected crack curving leftward to a bolt, then steps left and finishes past three additional bolts.
Begin on the wall's left side and climb the face beyond a horizontal crack plus a lone bolt, continuing straight to the top.
Edgy pockets in the yellow stone lead over the roof. A crack beneath the roof accepts a one-inch piece, and five bolts lead to the lower-off rings.
The moves low down are awkward, but overall it is a good climb for beginners.

moves.from: Gear to about two inches protects it.
